'''Álvaro Odriozola Arzallus''' ({{IPA|es|ˈalβaɾo oðɾjoˈθola}}; born 14 December 1995) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{Spanish football updater|Real Sociedad}} club [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/real-sociedad/20170116/413395192937/odriozola-un-punal-reconvertido-a-lateral.html|title=Odriozola, un puñal reconvertido a lateral|trans-title=Odriozola, a dagger converted into a full back|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|last=Isasa|first=Xabier|language=es|date=16 January 2017|accessdate=17 January 2017}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Real Sociedad===
[[file:Álvaro Odriozola.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Odriozola with Real Sociedad in 2017]]
Born in [[San Sebastián]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], Odriozola joined [[Real Sociedad]]'s youth setup in 2006, at the age of ten.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-sociedad/2017/01/17/587dfd7b46163f20138b4585.html|title=Odriozola tuvo el debut soñado en Primera|trans-title=Odriozola had the debut of his dreams in ''Primera''|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|last=Badallo|first=Óscar|language=es|date=17 January 2017|accessdate=17 January 2017}}</ref> On 1 September 2013 he made his senior debut with [[Real Sociedad B|the reserves]], starting in a 3–0 [[Segunda División B]] away loss against [[UD Las Palmas Atlético]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realsociedad.com/document/view/spa/0/167283/el-sanse-cae-ante-la-ud-las-palmas-atletico|title=El Sanse cae ante la UD Las Palmas Atlético (3–0)|trans-title=Sanse fall against UD Las Palmas Atlético (3–0)|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=1 September 2013|accessdate=17 January 2017}}</ref> and in the same month made the first of several appearances in the [[UEFA Youth League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.noticiasdegipuzkoa.com/2017/03/20/la-real/asoma-la-generacion-del-95?random=648103|title=Asoma la generación del 95|trans-title=The generation of 95 arrives|newspaper=Noticias de Gipuzkoa|last=Rodrigo|first=Marco|language=es|date=20 March 2017|accessdate=25 August 2017|archive-date=25 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825184946/http://www.noticiasdegipuzkoa.com/2017/03/20/la-real/asoma-la-generacion-del-95?random=648103|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Players-And-Staff/The-Academy/Academy-News/2013/Oct/real-sociedad-v-manchester-united-uefa-youth-league-report.aspx|title=U19: Utd 0 Sociedad 1|publisher=Manchester United F.C|date=23 October 2013|accessdate=25 August 2017}}</ref>

Odriozola was promoted to the B-side ahead of the [[2014–15 Segunda División B|2014–15 season]], and scored his first goal on 6 September 2014 by netting the last in a 3–0 home win against [[Real Unión]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realsociedad.com/document/view/spa/225/178480/el-sanse-se-lleva-con-claridad-el-derbi-ante-el-real-union-(3-0)|title=El Sanse se lleva con claridad el derbi ante el Real Unión (3–0)|trans-title=Sanse clearly win the derby against Real Unión (3–0)|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=6 September 2014|accessdate=17 January 2017}}</ref> On 25 February 2016, he renewed his contract with ''Sanse'' until 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realsociedad.com/document/view/spa/225/197463/bautista--zubeldia--odriozola-and-sangalli-renew-with-real-sociedad-|title=Bautista, Zubeldia, Odriozola and Sangalli renew with Real Sociedad|publisher=Real Sociedad|date=25 February 2016|accessdate=17 January 2017}}</ref>

On 16 January 2017, as both [[Carlos Martínez (footballer, born April 1986)|Carlos Martínez]] and [[Joseba Zaldúa]] were injured, Odriozola made his first-team – and [[La Liga]] – debut by starting in a 2–0 away win against [[Málaga CF]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2016_17/la-liga/jornada_18/mga_rso/|title=Esta Real sí araña|trans-title=This Real can scratch|newspaper=Marca|last=Egea|first=Pablo|language=es|date=16 January 2017|accessdate=17 January 2017}}</ref> Up to the end of [[2016–17 La Liga|the campaign]], he played in a further 16 competitive matches.<ref name=bdf/>

Odriozola renewed his contract until 2022 on 10 June 2017, and was definitively promoted to the senior squad ahead of the [[2017–18 La Liga|2017–18 season]], quickly becoming the first-choice right-back.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2018/05/01/real-sociedad/909989-odriozola-volvera-a-la-titularidad.html|title=Odriozola volverá a la titularidad|trans-title=Odriozola will return to starting lineup|publisher=Vavel|last=Chozas|first=José Alberto|language=es|date=1 May 2018|accessdate=4 June 2018}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 15 February 2018, in the 2–2 draw with [[FC Red Bull Salzburg]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]] [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League|round of 32]] at [[Anoeta Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cuatro.com/deportes/futbol/Cronica-Real-Sociedad-Salzburgo_0_2516326216.html|title=Crónica del Real Sociedad – Salzburgo, 2–2|trans-title=Real Sociedad – Salzburg match report, 2–2|publisher=[[Cuatro (TV channel)|Cuatro]]|language=es|date=15 February 2018|accessdate=20 July 2018}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:2023 05 06 Final de la Copa del Rey - 52879024229 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Odriozola with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], celebrating the win of the 2023 [[Copa del Rey]]]]

On 5 July 2018, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] reached an agreement with Real Sociedad for the transfer of Odriozola.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/07/official-announcement-alvaro-odriozola|title=Official announcement: Álvaro Odriozola|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=5 July 2018|accessdate=5 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/en/news/details/agreement-for-the-transfer-to-real-madrid|title=Agreement for the transfer to Real Madrid|publisher=Real Sociedad|date=5 July 2018|accessdate=5 July 2018}}</ref> The fee was reported to be €30 million, plus €5 million of conditional add-ons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/real-madrid/official-real-madrid-sign-alvaro-odriozola-6927498|title=Official: Real Madrid sign Alvaro Odriozola|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|date=5 July 2018|accessdate=5 July 2018}}</ref> He made his debut on 22 September, playing the full 90 minutes in a 1–0 win over [[RCD Espanyol]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/09/22/5ba6a900e2704ee9af8b45e2.html|title=Asensio the difference against a dogged Espanyol|newspaper=Marca|last=Pettigrove|first=Jason|date=22 September 2018|accessdate=23 September 2018}}</ref> Odriozola scored his first league goal on 21 April 2021, scoring the second goal in a 3–0 win over [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid go top as Sevilla keep up title charge |url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-04/22/c_139897670.htm |access-date=22 April 2021 |agency=Xinhua |date=22 April 2021}}</ref>

==== Loan to Bayern Munich ====
After playing just five times for Madrid during the first half of 2019–20.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51206594|title=Bayern Munich sign Real Madrid defender Alvaro Odriozola on loan|date=22 January 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=22 January 2020|language=en-gb}}</ref> In January 2020, Odriozola was loaned to [[Bundesliga]] club [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://fcbayern.com/en/news/2020/01/bayern-sign-alvaro-odriozola-on-loan|title=Bayern sign Álvaro Odriozola on loan|publisher=fcbayern.com|date=22 January 2020|accessdate=22 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/22/official-announcement-odriozola|title=Official Announcement: Odriozola|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=22 January 2020|accessdate=22 January 2020}}</ref> On 23 August 2020, he won the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League]] with Bayern Munich.<ref name="CL">{{Cite news|date=23 August 2020|title=Paris St-Germain 0–1 Bayern Munich: German side win Champions League final|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53867676|access-date=23 August 2020}}</ref>

==== Loan to Fiorentina ====
On 28 August 2021, Odriozola joined [[Serie A]] club [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Álvaro Odriozola|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/08/28/official-announcement-alvaro-odriozola|access-date=28 August 2021|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=28 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Odriozola signs for Fiorentina|url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2021-08-28/odriozola-signs-for-fiorentina|access-date=28 August 2021|publisher=acffiorentina.com|date=28 August 2021|archive-date=30 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830020950/https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2021-08-28/odriozola-signs-for-fiorentina|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Return to Real Sociedad===
On 1 September 2023, Real Sociedad announced the return of Odriozola on a six-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/es/noticias/detalle/de-vuelta-en-casa-1|title=Vuelve a casa|trans-title=Returns home|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=1 September 2023|accessdate=1 September 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Odriozola was first selected to play for [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21s]] by [[Albert Celades]], helping the squad reach the final of the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2017 UEFA European Championship]]. He earned his first full [[Cap (sports)|cap]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 6 October 2017, in a 3–0 win over [[Albania national football team|Albania]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group G|qualifiers]]; he played the entire match, and also provided an [[Assist (football)|assist]] for [[Thiago Alcântara]]'s goal as the team reached the finals as group winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/match/2017798--spain-vs-albania/|title=Spain 3–0 Albania|publisher=UEFA|date=6 October 2017|access-date=7 October 2017}}</ref>

Odriozola was named in the 23-man squad for the finals in Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=21 May 2018|accessdate=21 May 2018}}</ref> He scored his first goal for his country on 3 June 2018, in a 1–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] draw with [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in [[Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/article212455854.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142405/http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/article212455854.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 June 2018|title=Spain held by Switzerland ahead of World Cup|newspaper=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=3 June 2018|accessdate=3 June 2018}}</ref>
